the model says the meaning changed: The diff clears the pending full run and empties the unverified-tests list when a green full run of the merged tree exists, so tests that never ran or have no passing run no longer hold the merge, which the requirement and DEC-404 say they must.; filed as a question for the owner, to ask with the question tool: The requirement still agrees with what you asked for: the merge is the one hold, and it stops on failing tests. You also decided that a test with no passing run, or a pending full run, holds the merge too.

The change adds a shortcut. If any checkout on this machine has recorded a green full run of exactly the merged code, the pending full run is cleared and the list of tests with no passing run is emptied without being checked. Failing tests and regressions still hold.

What is unclear is whether you wanted this. It may fit your decision, because a green full run of the same code should mean every test passed, and it avoids running the suite again. But the merge now assumes that run covered every test instead of checking each one, so a test the run skipped or left out would no longer hold the merge. The requirement also doesn't say that a run from another checkout counts.

No example in the requirement clearly breaks, and no owner request is on record for this turn, so I can't tell if the change was intended.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Keep the change and reword the requirement to say a green full run of exactly the merged code, from any checkout on this machine, clears the pending run and the never-run tests") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Keep the shortcut for the pending full run only, and still check each test for a passing run") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Undo the change, so only this checkout's own evidence can clear these holds") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (plumb stale card SR-260#3 --consequences "..." --why "...")
